investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent evals (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — leaving all four required evidence fields missing and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes. No preemption victims were available, and the 4 remaining nodes were excluded by node affinity/selector rules. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~139–145 seconds before the probe timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an eval runner or contract misconfiguration. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-peer-pod nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently limited to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are undersized or their VM resource limit is set too low, any concurrent load will exhaust capacity.

Tertiary — resource leak from prior eval runs: if previous remote-agent pods were not cleaned up (e.g., withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs did not complete), their kata.peerpods.io/vm slots may still be held, reducing available capacity for new probes.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node restart, maintenance cordon): one or both peer-pod nodes may have been temporarily unavailable or cordoned, reducing effective capacity to zero at the time of the eval run. No cordon or maintenance signal is present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: Remote Agents eval failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion prevents pod scheduling across all three remote-agent checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the same eval run because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM on any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message) confirms no schedulable node existed at eval time. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). The pod remained Unschedulable for ~145 s before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and a full contract gap for orgId, agentId, readyState, and state (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-30T23:43–23:45Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place agent pods: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption was possible. The eval runner never reached the agent creation step, so zero evidence fields were collected and the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-layer signal of a Kubernetes infrastructure constraint; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption yielding no victims, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. The eval runner calls createAgent() (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) which triggers pod creation; because the pod never schedules, the agent never becomes reachable, and the probe times out after ~145s returning no evidence. The root cause is a Kubernetes-layer resource exhaustion on kata.peerpods.io/vm, not an application code defect.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent evals (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — leaving all four required evidence fields missing and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes. No preemption victims were available, and the 4 remaining nodes were excluded by node affinity/selector rules. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~139–145 seconds before the probe timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an eval runner or contract misconfiguration. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-peer-pod nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently limited to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are undersized or their VM resource limit is set too low, any concurrent load will exhaust capacity.

Tertiary — resource leak from prior eval runs: if previous remote-agent pods were not cleaned up (e.g., withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs did not complete), their kata.peerpods.io/vm slots may still be held, reducing available capacity for new probes.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node restart, maintenance cordon): one or both peer-pod nodes may have been temporarily unavailable or cordoned, reducing effective capacity to zero at the time of the eval run. No cordon or maintenance signal is present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

[Likely] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata-capable nodes), and those nodes are saturated — the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible.
[Possible] A recent scale-down, node failure, or maintenance event reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a higher count to 2, shrinking available vm slots below the demand level.
[Possible] Leaked or stuck agent pods from prior eval runs (or other workloads) are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations and not releasing them, exhausting the resource pool.
[Less likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node was reduced via a configuration change, lowering total cluster capacity without a corresponding node count increase.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl node describe showing kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is not exhausted on the two eligible nodes would disprove resource exhaustion as the cause.

A successful re-run of any remote-agent check that returns a scheduled pod and non-empty evidence (orgId, agentId, etc.) would indicate the failure was transient rather than a persistent resource constraint.
Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude previously eligible nodes would shift the root cause from resource exhaustion to a misconfiguration.
Scheduler logs showing a different rejection reason (e.g., image pull failure, quota exceeded) for the same pods would disprove the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion hypothesis.

A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state concurrent with this failure window would suggest the issue is intermittent or isolated to specific pod requests rather than cluster-wide exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm available capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add an eval that detects stuck Pending remote-agent pods older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60s) and reports them as a separate infrastructure health signal.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3 nodes), alerting when the eligible node pool shrinks.

Consider a canary eval that attempts a minimal remote-agent pod scheduling dry-run (without full agent startup) to detect Unschedulable conditions faster and with lower resource cost than the full runtime probe.
